messages.subject: Debugging invalidation
parts:
Is there a way to debug invalidation chains?

One of my reactives gets evaluated twice each time I update the inputs and I'm not sure why.

-Alex

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Re: Debugging invalidation
parts:
okay, looks like UI<-reactiveUI(...) depends upon reactiveVal$A and reactiveVal$B

reactiveVal$B depends upon reactiveVal$A

the reactiveUI is being invoked twice - once for old B and new A, and then for new B and new A.

How do I fix this ordering?  I want the observers building the reactiveValues to be executed before the reactiveUI?

Does Shiny construct a dependency graph to avoid double updating in this way?

-Alex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Debugging invalidation
parts:
No, we don't have a dependency graph. I don't think a dependency graph will help in this case (but you're more than welcome to try to prove otherwise). We avoid over-reactivity in most cases through lazy evaluation and deferred execution of observers, but not in the case of setting reactiveValues. When you go through reactiveValues, you're exiting the reactive framework and coming back in (since setting a reactive value is something that happens outside of the reactive graph--it's unintuitive but true).

Can you tell me what reactiveVal$A/B and the reactiveUI actually represent, so we can talk about whether there's another way to structure things?
